solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They say Rita's humour is warped

indicators.note: something warped is bent out of its true shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S counted as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that Rita has a twisted sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Rita's' is part of the fodder here, so the pool is RITAS plus HUMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce gossip, reporting what people are saying without vouching for it.

clue.text: Desert people engaged in fierce competition

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
a race is a people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Deserters and locals become caught up in a bitter struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a relentless struggle to get ahead at work, like rats racing for food.

clue.text: Animal's low points

definitions.note: read as 'the animal is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
S, south, is a compass point
E, east, is another compass point

explanation.surface: A remark on where some creature is at its weakest.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deer of northern forests, known in Europe as the elk.

clue.text: Such a joint may be found worldwide

definitions.meaning: a ... joint is a coupling that lets a shaft bend in any direction

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain kind of joint turns up all over the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means all-embracing, and the engineering term names a flexible shaft coupling.

clue.text: Sound cure for cant

indicators.note: sound here means said out loud, so the next word is replaced by one that is pronounced the same

parts.note: to cure is to heal

explanation.surface: A healthy remedy for hypocritical talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cant' looks like hypocritical talk but here is the verb meaning to tilt, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: To heel is to lean over to one side, as a ship tilting in the wind does.

clue.text: Indecision shows us soft in reason

indicators.note: in tells us the next pieces sit inside the word for reason

parts.note: sense is sound reason, as in talking sense
taken as written
P, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Being undecided proves we are weak in our thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty of waiting for an outcome not yet decided.

clue.text: She's a vessel in the drink

definitions.note: read as 'she is', a woman's name defining the answer

indicators.note: in places the ship inside the word for the drink

parts.note: tea is the drink, the British national brew
SS, steamship, is the abbreviation for a vessel

explanation.surface: A woman described as a ship sinking into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is usually the sea in crosswords; here it is literally TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, a short form of Theresa, defined simply as some female person.

clue.text: Elderly relative gives £1,000 to graduate

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A generous old family member hands a large cash gift to someone who has just finished university.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an older family member, two generations up.

clue.text: Composer has part written up for graduate

parts.note: J. S. Bach the German composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the word is entered bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A composer writes a part for a recent university leaver.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bachelor of Arts or Science holds a first university degree.

clue.text: A watch and a clock which can't be relied on?

definitions.meaning: a pair of timepieces, so two devices that keep time
people who are unfaithful to their partners, cheating on them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a pair of timepieces can be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Two timepieces count as a pair of devices that keep time; cheating partners are known as unfaithful lovers.

clue.text: Opera house presenting extract from Tosca last year

indicators.note: an extract is a piece taken out, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Milan theatre stages a piece of Puccini's Tosca, as it did last year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'year' is only surface colour: the letters run across 'Tosca last'.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is the world's most famous opera theatre.

clue.text: Exam refers to All about Eve

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word all goes around the name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A test question concerns the classic film All About Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced Level is the British school-leaving qualification taken around age eighteen.

clue.text: Retired, Edward longed to be free

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Having stopped work, Edward yearned for liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached means unattached, separated, loose from what held it.

clue.text: Realise she can make an anagram

indicators.note: the clue openly says the preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman realises she is able to rearrange letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realise' means to convert assets into money, not to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash is to turn a cheque or asset into cash, which is to realise its value.

clue.text: Silly Eton chap that has a situation in Whitehall

definitions.text: that has a situation in Whitehall

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are behaving foolishly and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish Old Etonian lands a post in government.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government offices, where the national war memorial stands; 'situation' means location, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The national war memorial stands in the middle of the street running past government offices in London.

clue.text: She is a beautiful Italian

parts.note: taken as written
bella is the Italian word for beautiful

explanation.surface: A woman described as a lovely Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so it can stand for any female person.

clue.text: Articles from a picnic basket one's found in the meadow

parts.note: butter is one item you might pack for a picnic
a cup is another item packed for a picnic

explanation.surface: Items unpacked from a hamper while someone sits in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow wild flower that grows in grassland and meadows.

clue.text: Money box that's opened daily in the kitchen

definitions.text: that's opened daily in the kitchen

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a bin is a container or box

explanation.surface: A cash box that gets opened every day in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen container for keeping loaves, opened whenever someone needs a slice.

clue.text: Letter left with nobleman

parts.note: and means together with
a lord is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A letter left behind along with a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not a message but one who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lets out property to tenants is literally one who lets, hence a letter.

clue.text: Co-operation as in oil refining

indicators.note: refining processes crude material into another form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Joint working, as practised in the oil-refining industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a working link between groups that co-ordinates their efforts.

clue.text: Goes hunting, we hear, for birds

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is replaced by one pronounced like it

parts.note: a hunter stalks prey

explanation.surface: Someone sets out after wildfowl, or so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike in a standard British accent, which drops the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Storks are large long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: He has to wait for a job

definitions.text: He has to wait for a job

parts.words: He has to wait for a job
parts.note: looks like someone idle between jobs, but describes one whose work is to wait at table

explanation.surface: An unemployed man must hang on until work comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic employee waits on the household, waiting being his job.

clue.text: It pushes up water rates in a reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation puts things into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Water charges rise after a council shake-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is one where pressure forces groundwater up without pumping.

clue.text: It could be a bit of a shock at harvest time

definitions.text: It could be a bit of a shock at harvest time

parts.words: It could be a bit of a shock at harvest time
parts.note: a shock is also a stook, a group of bundled corn stalks stood up in a field to dry

explanation.surface: Something mildly startling happens when the crops are brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle of cut corn stalks, several of which are stood together to make a stook.

clue.text: Material on display requires renovation

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
to air something is to show it, so an airing is a display

explanation.surface: Fabric on show needs mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair is the fixing or restoring of something damaged, the work of renovation.

clue.text: Bail set before one delivers excuse

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A defendant offers a justification once bail has been fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea of having been elsewhere at the time, used to excuse the accused.

clue.text: Twice reduced by 50%

parts.note: two times cut in half leaves one time

explanation.surface: Something is cut in half and then halved again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests halving twice; instead the word for two times is halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of two occasions is a single occasion, a solitary time.

clue.text: Musician wants a meal right away

indicators.note: away means taken off, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A performer wants to eat immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of operettas. 'Right away' looks like 'at once' but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé was a nineteenth-century composer, best known for the Light Cavalry overture.

clue.text: Skeleton service?

parts.note: a skeleton service is a minimal one, but read as a dinner set made of bones

explanation.surface: Wondering about a reduced, minimum-staff operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The porcelain is made with ash from animal bones, so a dinner service of it is a skeleton one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain made with bone ash, used for tableware sets.

clue.text: Only a personal impression but admissible as evidence

definitions.text: Only a personal impression but admissible as evidence

parts.words: Only a personal impression but admissible as evidence
parts.note: looks like a subjective opinion, but the impression is one left by a finger

explanation.surface: A mere subjective opinion is nonetheless accepted in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The mark left by a fingertip is unique to each person and used in court to identify them.
